title: U.S. House · Colorado's 2nd District
area: North-central Colorado, including Boulder, Fort Collins and the western mountain corridor.

context.text: Incumbent Joe Neguse advanced unopposed from the Democratic primary. Kelley Dennison defeated Christina Blunt in the Republican primary. This seat is a Democratic stronghold.

candidates.name: Joe Neguse
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, unopposed

summary.text: Joe Neguse is the Democratic incumbent representing Colorado's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2018. He serves as House Democratic Assistant Leader and previously served on the University of Colorado Board of Regents.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree and a law degree from the University of Colorado.
Co-founded New Era Colorado, a youth civic-engagement organization.
Elected to the University of Colorado Board of Regents (2008-2014).
Appointed executive director of Colorado's Department of Regulatory Agencies (2015-2017).

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Federal Lands Subcommittee), Committee on Judiciary, and Committee on Rules in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: As a sitting member of Congress, detailed floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script; this entry focuses on committee roles per the research assignment's division of labor.

summary.text: Kelley Dennison is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 2nd Congressional District. She is a Colorado native and small-business owner who describes her platform as focused on affordability, environmental stewardship of Colorado's headwaters, and pro-family policy.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Estes Park High School.
Graduated from the Academy of Natural Therapy in 2023.
Career experience includes working as a massage therapist and business owner.

priorities.text: Economic affordability: cites rising housing costs, gas, inflation and property taxes, and proposes strengthening small businesses and easing barriers to home ownership.
Environmental stewardship of Colorado's headwaters, rivers and forests, favoring 'responsible' land use and locally rooted stewardship over what she calls top-down mandates.
Pro-family policy, including protecting parental rights in education and health care decisions and support for veterans and seniors.

positions.summary: Calls for making it easier for families to afford homes while also favoring 'responsible' economic growth and locally-rooted land-use policy rather than top-down mandates.
Lists 'parental rights in education' as a passion area, favoring parents as informed and empowered partners in children's education decisions.

summary.text: Gaylon Kent is running in the general election for U.S. House Colorado District 2 on the Libertarian Party ballot line.
